description: Maintain a fixed-universe set with Briggs–Torczon dense and sparse inverse arrays, constant-time updates and clears.

source.title: An Efficient Representation for Sparse Sets
source.reference: ACM Letters on Programming Languages and Systems 2(1–4), 59–69 (1993).
source.implementation_status: Clean-room bounded ports from the published representation; no paper source code copied.

opcode_meaning.3: clear set; key must be zero

output.answer_bits: One bit per operation in trace order; insert/erase/contains return whether they changed/found the key, and clear returns whether the set was nonempty before clearing.
output.final_membership_mask: Bit k is set iff key k is in the final set.

contract.membership_test: present(x) iff sparse[x] < size and dense[sparse[x]] == x.
contract.insert: Append a missing key to dense[size], record sparse[key]=size, then increment size; duplicate insert leaves the set unchanged.
contract.erase: For a present key, move dense[size-1] into its dense slot, repair that key's sparse back-pointer, then decrement size. The old sparse entry is left stale and fails the membership predicate.
contract.clear: Set size to zero and leave sparse entries untouched; every old entry fails the size-bound test.
contract.initialization: Initialize sparse entries for the declared universe to universe_size, a sentinel outside every valid dense index.

complexity.construction: O(universe_size) to initialize the bounded sparse index.
